correctness.rationale: With 0<r<1 and positive integers k,d, the signed Fourier convolution is the geometric Green function applied to sources at the specified knots. Its homogeneous recurrence between knots has the claimed two endpoint weights (strictly positive at interior integer positions); after dk it is a decaying geometric tail. The coarse-grid precision formula gives the three inverse rows including the reflected left boundary and the right endpoint, also for d=1. Bochner then identifies the cone with the orthant. The ray supports give ranks 2k-1 and 4k-2 for the first and inner rays, respectively, and the final ray has an infinite tail. If u_d=0 the spectrum is finite; if u_d>0 a consecutive block from the tail gives an invertible Vandermonde matrix on any finite set of distinct sites. Uniform RKHS density is equivalent to full Fourier support, because characters with positive coefficients lie in the RKHS and each missing coefficient is detected by a continuous Fourier functional. Independent rational round-trip, interpolation and ray checks passed 21,660 assertions at three radii, k=1–4 and d=1–5; the supplied code was inspected, not run. The finite checks supplement the all-parameter proof.
